generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: When two extensible classes share the same structural shape, finite examples from either class can make absence from one enumeration act as false evidence for the other class.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Use finite negative vocabulary plus default accept for unknown members, or finite positive vocabulary plus default reject, while tests draw both sides from those same enumerations.
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: For bidirectional open classes sharing a structure, require unseen valid and unseen invalid members whose full literals are absent from production enumerations, vary at least one structural dimension, and run collision checks against nearby valid members; absence from either finite list is never semantic evidence.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Inventory positive and negative finite sources, attack both sides with unseen members, verify attack literals are not hardcoded, and prove explicit affirmative discriminants rather than default behavior carry the decision.

transfer_cases.evidence: Synthetic control admits a valid unseen extension and rejects an unseen incompatible extension sharing the same route shape without adding either literal to finite registries.
Synthetic control separates unseen accepted and denied labels in the same wrapper shape using affirmative evidence and a collision sibling.
